name: AI SEO Masterclass - Introduction Why AI SEO Is Not Optional
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-08

# Summary
The opening lesson argues that AI search (GEO) is "just SEO with new distribution layers": ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews now answer questions directly and cite a handful of sources, so a brand that is not cited is invisible to those searchers. The author (Jacky Chou, Indexsy / LocalRank.so) frames 2026 as an early-adopter window.

# Key concepts
- AI engines synthesize one answer and cite the brands they trust; ranking a blue link is no longer the whole game.
- Usage claims cited: ChatGPT 400M+ weekly users (late 2025), Perplexity 15M+ monthly users, AI Overviews on 1.5B+ queries per day.
- Ahrefs study of 26,283 cited URLs (the course's core data point):
  - 43.8% of ChatGPT citations come from "Best X" listicles.
  - 79.1% of cited content was updated in the current year.
  - Low-DR sites can be cited; structure beats raw domain authority.
- Traditional SEO still matters because AI models crawl the same web.

# Action items from the lesson
1. Check GA4 referrals for chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai and other "chat" sources to set an AI-traffic baseline.
2. Start a brand-mention log: search "brand + best" in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google.
3. Calendar a monthly refresh of the top 10 pages (date, statistics, 200 to 500 new words).

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Freshness is the cheapest lever: Summit AZ, Pipeliners and Alphalete blogs and city pages can get a scheduled refresh rhythm, logged so results can be measured.
- AI-referral baselines fit the existing visibility work in [SEO Tracker](lib:brain-seo-tracker) (LLM visibility from [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas)).
- The revenue figures in this lesson are the author's own claims, not verified data.
